originalTitle: Karnataka Bank Q1 profit jumps 43% as asset quality improves
simplifiedContent: Karnataka Bank just released its quarterly financial results, and they're looking good. The bank's profit increased by 43% compared to the same time last year, reaching Rs 419 crore. This is mainly because the bank's business is growing, it has fewer bad loans, and it didn't have to set aside as much money for potential losses. The bank also saw increases in the money it makes from interest on loans and its overall operating profit. This is a positive sign for the bank's financial health and performance.

originalTitle: Copper slips ahead of Fed rate decision, aluminium rises on Gulf fighting
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the price of copper is going down because investors are being careful before the Federal Reserve announces its decision on interest rates. Prices are also being affected by China having more copper available, which means there's less demand. On the other hand, the price of aluminium is going up because of concerns that fighting in the Middle East might disrupt supplies. This matters because changes in the prices of these metals can affect the companies that use or produce them, and ultimately impact the overall stock market. The interest rate decision by the Federal Reserve is also important because it can influence the entire economy.

originalTitle: US Treasury yields rise after three-day fall as oil jumps, Fed decision looms
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the interest rates on US government loans (called Treasury yields) went up after falling for three days. This happened because oil prices jumped up, which makes people worry about inflation (prices rising too fast). The Federal Reserve, which controls interest rates, is making a decision today, and traders think they will keep interest rates the same for now. However, traders expect interest rates to go up in September and possibly again before the end of the year, which is why they're paying close attention to what the Federal Reserve does. This matters because changes in interest rates can affect the overall economy and stock market.

originalTitle: Manipal Health Enterprises IPO off to slow start, subscribed 15% on opening day; retail portion booked 27%
simplifiedContent: Manipal Health Enterprises, a company, is trying to raise money by selling its shares to the public, which is called an Initial Public Offering (IPO). On the first day, not many people showed interest, with only 15% of the shares being subscribed, or bought. However, individual investors, also known as retail investors, were a bit more interested, with 27% of the shares set aside for them being booked. The company had already raised ₹4,167 crore from big investors before the IPO even started. The shares are expected to start trading on the stock market on August 5.

originalTitle: US stock market today: Wall Street futures inch higher ahead of Fed decision; Middle East tensions resurface
simplifiedContent: The US stock market is expecting some news from the Federal Reserve, which is making investors a bit cautious. Because of this, the stock market is moving slowly, with some parts (like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq) going up slightly (0.2%) and others (like the Dow) going down. This means that investors are being careful and not making big changes until they hear what the Federal Reserve decides. The Federal Reserve's decision is important because it can affect the overall direction of the stock market. The market's slow movement shows that investors are waiting to see what happens next before making any big moves.

originalTitle: US Treasury yields rise as markets await Fed rate decision
simplifiedContent: The US Treasury yields, which is a measure of how much the government pays to borrow money, have started to rise again after falling for a few days. This is because investors are waiting to see what the Federal Reserve, the central bank of the US, will decide to do with interest rates. The yields had fallen recently, but are still expected to be higher this month than usual, partly because of concerns about inflation (which is the rate at which prices are rising) due to higher oil prices. This matters because it can affect how much it costs to borrow money, and it can also impact the overall economy. The increase in yields suggests that investors are preparing for potential changes in interest rates, which will be decided by the Federal Reserve soon.
